fields.meta_title: Presentation Evaluation Form With Rubric Scores | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a presentation evaluation form that scores talks against your rubric and sends each presenter the results. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Presentation Evaluation Form That Tallies the Scores
fields.hero_description: Build a presentation evaluation form that totals the rubric, averages peer ratings, and saves each score to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Scores That Go Somewhere After the Talk
fields.features_subheading: A paper rubric waits in a stack until someone adds it up. As a form, each evaluation is totaled on submit and saved as a row.
fields.feature_1:
Rubric totals worked out on submit

Each criterion gets its own 1 to 5 scale and a line describing what a 5 looks like. The app adds up the criteria the moment the evaluator submits, and nobody totals a sheet by hand.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that change with who is scoring

A teacher sees the full rubric, and a classmate sees two ratings and a comment box. Evaluators pick a role on the first screen, and the form shows only the questions for that role.
fields.feature_3:
Results emailed to each presenter

When scoring closes, the app emails each presenter their total, the score on every criterion, and the comments on their talk. You decide whether evaluator names go with the comments.
fields.feature_4:
Peer ratings averaged per group member

After a group presentation, teammates rate one another's contribution. The app averages the ratings each member receives and alerts the instructor when one drops below your line.
fields.feature_5:
A QR code on the closing slide

Audience members scan the code and rate the talk on a phone, one question per screen. Every rating lands in the session's table, and there is no cap on how many people respond.
fields.feature_6:
Code on GitHub, scores in your database

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when a school or company wants the form running on its own servers. The scores themselves stay in a database you own.
fields.why_description: A rubric template hands you the criteria. Emergent builds the scoring behind them and keeps each evaluation in a database you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
By the last bell, Nico has his 17 out of 20

Hedda Larrabee teaches 10th-grade history at Mossbank High School and scores each talk on her tablet while the student is still speaking. Her rubric has 4 criteria worth 5 points each. Nico Albescu's talk on the Erie Canal earns 17 out of 20, and the app emails him the score and her comment before the last bell.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every speaker hears from the room by Monday

The Prairie Soil Health Summit puts a QR code on the last slide of every session. After Delphine Arceneaux's talk on cover crops, 46 attendees rate its content and delivery from 1 to 5 on their phones. The Monday after the summit, the app emails her the session's averages: 4.6 for content and 4.1 for delivery.
fields.tab_content_3:
A peer average under 3 goes to the instructor

Renata Sobczak's marketing students present in groups of 4 and rate their 3 teammates' contribution from 1 to 5. The app averages what each student receives. Cole Pettersen, in the group that pitched a campus coffee cart, averages 2.3, and Renata gets his name and his teammates' comments before grades post.
fields.tab_content_4:
Trainers who differ by 7 points talk it over

Osprey Point Freight ends its new-manager program with a 10-minute capstone talk that two trainers score on their own. Rob Feeney gives Bettina Kroll 22 out of 30, and Asha Venkataraman gives her 15 out of 30. A gap over 5 points holds the score, and the app emails both trainers to agree on one number.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable rubric sheets (a medical school PDF, sample PDFs, fillable-PDF sites) and template galleries (Jotform, AidaForm, Typeform, a feedback template site), and each one stops at the criteria. This page shows what the scores do after submit: a rubric total emailed to the student the same day, each conference speaker sent their own session's ratings, peer ratings inside a presenting group averaged and flagged to the instructor, and two trainers' scores compared before a training score counts, with Carnegie Mellon's teaching guidance on rubrics and peer evaluation quoted where it applies.
tab_stories: Hedda Larrabee scores each 10th-grade history talk at Mossbank High School on 4 criteria worth 5 points each from her tablet, and the app emails Nico Albescu his 17 out of 20 with her comment before the last bell.

The Prairie Soil Health Summit puts a QR code on every closing slide, 46 attendees rate Delphine Arceneaux's session on content and delivery, and the app emails her that session's results the Monday after the summit.

Renata Sobczak's marketing students present in groups of 4 and rate their 3 teammates on contribution, and the app sends her any student whose peer average falls below 3, which is how Cole Pettersen's 2.3 reaches her before grades post.

Osprey Point Freight has two trainers score each new manager's capstone talk out of 30, and when Rob Feeney gives Bettina Kroll 22 and Asha Venkataraman gives her 15, the 7-point gap holds the score until the trainers talk.
